summary.headline: GFL Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 45% YoY to INR1,760 crores, with EBITDA up 32% to INR473 crores at a steady 27% margin.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue was INR1,760 crores (+45% YoY, +11% QoQ) and EBITDA INR473 crores (+32% YoY, +11% QoQ), with PAT of INR240 crores (+42% YoY). Fluorochemicals revenue more than doubled YoY to INR607 crores, led by R-32 refrigerants, while fluoropolymers grew 22% YoY to INR931 crores. Battery materials (GFCL EV) remains pre-commercial, with LiPF6 ramping and LFP, electrolyte and anode timelines pushed out, and the INR6,000 crore battery capex plan is being funded partly by external equity still to be raised.

financial_highlights.change: +22% YoY (vs INR764 crores), +2% QoQ (vs INR914 crores)
+135% YoY (vs INR258 crores), +33% QoQ (vs INR458 crores)
-5% YoY (vs INR158 crores), -8% QoQ (vs INR164 crores)

segments.name: Fluoropolymers
segments.commentary: Revenue INR931 crores, +22% YoY, against guidance of 17-20% annual growth; management says growth is volume-led plus higher value from approved advanced-application grades (FKM, PSA, modified PTFE for semiconductors and data centres).

segments.name: Fluorochemicals (refrigerants)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR607 crores, +135% YoY, driven by R-32; management expects initial R-32 capacity to be fully utilised by end of Q3 FY27 and R-134A production to start by Q4 FY27. Refrigerant demand and pricing described as stable near term.

segments.name: Bulk chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR151 crores, -5% YoY and -8% QoQ, due to lower caustic soda prices and higher captive use of chloromethanes for R-32.

segments.name: Advanced battery materials (GFCL EV)
segments.commentary: Pre-commercial; LiPF6 supplied to 5 global electrolyte players with volume-linked, formula-priced contracts. Revenue from LFP, electrolyte and anode is pushed out; no revenue figure disclosed in the call.

guidance_outlook: Fluoropolymers: sustain 17-20% annual growth; capex to follow volume plans, with new polymerisation reactors taking about 8-10 months.
R-32: initial planned capacity fully utilised by end of Q3 FY27; R-134A commercial production by Q4 FY27 (management says on track).
Battery materials commercial supplies under long-term agreements to begin from Q4 FY27.
LiPF6: expanded capacity expected to reach full utilisation by Q1 FY28; salt capacities near full utilisation by Q1/Q2 FY28.
Electrolyte: domestic demand expected to ramp from mid-CY27; revenue expected in H2 FY28; no new electrolyte capacity planned for about 6 months.
LFP: significant capacity to come online around Q3 FY28 or end FY28, with revenue impact at end FY28 or start FY29. Oman project put on hold and shifted to India.
Battery capex: INR2,100 crore FY27 plan slips about 1.5 quarters; part of the INR6,000 crore total. Management retains 2x asset turn and 25% EBITDA margin guidance for battery business.
Non-battery capex: about INR800 crore FY27 plan, roughly half complete at the end of Q2.
capex_capacity: Battery materials capex plan INR6,000 crores in total; FY27 allocation INR2,100 crores, now expected to spill over by about 1.5 quarters into FY28; Oman LFP project on hold with capacity moved to India.
Non-battery capex about INR800 crores for FY27 (includes fluoropolymers), roughly half complete after Q2.
Anode project slowed and placed on hold to prioritise LFP, electrolyte and salt; backward integration capex to follow once downstream capacity is utilised.
Fluoropolymers debottlenecking underway; additional growth capex planned over the next 1 year; monomer capacity in place, polymerisation reactors being added.
Electronic chemicals plant at Janiadara in early conceptual stage; product and capex not disclosed.
demand_pricing: Fluoropolymer growth attributed to both volume and higher realisations from advanced-application approvals; demand traction cited in EV, semiconductors, data centres and green hydrogen.

LiPF6 contracts are formula-linked to lithium prices, with pass-through of raw material moves; management says margins remain protected despite China LiPF6 price falling from about INR150,000 to about INR100,000 per tonne (as quoted by analyst).
Refrigerant demand supported by transition to lower-GWP refrigerants; R-32 air-conditioning adoption cited.
Export-led battery revenue expected in FY28, with domestic demand ramping mid-CY27 onward; 3 domestic battery manufacturers currently at production level and all engaged by GFCL.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the fluoropolymer 22% growth is volume versus price, and is 20% growth sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Kapil Malhotra said the 22% growth is volume-led and also reflects higher value from newly approved applications, and that growth momentum is expected to continue for a couple of years.

qa_highlights.question: When will R-32 reach peak utilisation and when does R-134A start?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr Kapoor said initial R-32 capacity will be fully utilised by end of Q3 FY27 and R-134A production is on track for Q4 FY27; no utilisation percentage was given.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR3,000+ crore FY27 capex be split and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said non-battery capex of INR800 crores is about halfway done, battery capex of INR2,100 crores is slipping about 1.5 quarters, and the total battery plan remains INR6,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR6,000 crore battery capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Akhil Jindal said about INR3,200 crores is already raised (INR2,300 crores equity, INR900 crores debt); the remaining plan is about INR1,500 crores debt, INR3,000-3,500 crores total equity and about INR1,000 crores from accruals; equity to be raised gradually over 12-24 months with no parent backstop.

qa_highlights.question: Why is electrolyte and anode revenue timing later, and what is the sequence?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said electrolyte revenue expected in H2 FY28, LFP large capacity contributing from end FY28 or early FY29, and anode later as it has been placed on hold.

qa_highlights.question: Will LiPF6 price declines in China affect pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr Kapoor said prices are linked to lithium and adders, most contracts pass through raw material changes, and margins remain protected.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2x asset turn and 25% EBITDA margin battery guidance still valid after shifting Oman capacity to India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is holding to the earlier guidance of 2x asset turn and 25% EBITDA margin.

risks_watch: Battery ramp-up delays: FY27 battery capex slips about 1.5 quarters and anode is on hold; revenue from LFP, electrolyte and anode is pushed to FY28-FY29.
Funding: about INR1,200 crores of equity still to be raised over 18-24 months, plus about INR1,500 crores of debt; no parent or promoter backstop.
Lithium-linked LiPF6 price deflation (China prices reportedly down sharply in the last month) could affect realisations if pass-through lags.
Bulk chemicals revenue decline from lower caustic soda prices and captive chloromethane use.
Watch: R-32 full utilisation by Q3 FY27, R-134A start by Q4 FY27, and first long-term battery supply revenue in Q4 FY27.
Electronic chemicals plant at Janiadara: capex and product details still undisclosed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on core chemicals growth and refrigerant volumes, but cautious and somewhat defensive on battery materials, where timelines for LFP, electrolyte and anode have slipped and several answers were left open.
key_quotes: Chemical segment revenue increased 42% year-on-year to INR1,723 crores, reflecting a healthy demand across the fluoropolymers and fluorochemicals portfolio.
Fluoropolymers business continued to deliver healthy growth, while fluorochemicals witnessed a particularly strong performance during the quarter.
Fortunately or unfortunately, our revenues are tied up to the end product ramp-up where we have seen some delays.
So we are still targeting what we had indicated earlier on battery materials, which is investment of INR 6,000 crores.

adds.what: New fluoropolymer polymerisation reactors (debottlenecking; monomer capacity already in place)
Initial R-32 refrigerant capacity (fully utilised by end Q3 FY27)
LiPF6 expanded capacity (full utilisation by Q1 FY28)
LFP battery materials capacity (significant, moved from Oman to India)

growth.why: Fluoropolymers guided at 17-20% annual growth (held) and R-32 initial capacity fully utilised by end Q3 FY27, but battery revenue and capex timelines slipped (INR2,100 crore FY27 battery capex spills about 1.5 quarters; commercial battery supplies pushed to Q4 FY27), with no explicit revenue growth % guided.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA margin held at 27% (steady QoQ) and management says LiPF6 margins are protected by pass-through, but battery margin guidance of 25% is not yet earning revenue and bulk chemicals fell 8% QoQ.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Initial R-32 capacity is commissioned and fully utilised by end Q3 FY27, R-134A production starts Q4 FY27 (on track), and LiPF6 expanded capacity is already commissioned with full utilisation by Q1 FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Fluoropolymers guided at 17-20% annual growth (Q2 delivered +22% YoY, volume-led), Fluorochemicals revenue more than doubled to INR607 crores (+135% YoY), and R-32 is filling up by Q3 FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Fluoropolymer polymerisation reactors are being added with growth capex planned over the next 1 year, and the INR2,100 crore FY27 battery capex and ~INR800 crore non-battery plan are in motion, though the battery plan is slipping about 1.5 quarters.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held fluoropolymer 17-20% growth and battery guidance, and the battery timelines slipped, so no clear basis for a raise is visible in the call.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Battery capex slips about 1.5 quarters, battery commercial supply cut to Q4 FY27, and LFP revenue pushed to end FY28/FY29, with about INR1,200 crore equity and INR1,500 crore debt still to be raised.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: R-134A production is on track to start by Q4 FY27 and first long-term battery supplies (LiPF6 to 5 global electrolyte players) are slated from Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Battery supply contracts with domestic manufacturers
rows.why: LiPF6 is supplied to 5 global electrolyte players on volume-linked contracts, 3 domestic battery makers are at production level and engaged, and electrolyte revenue is expected in H2 FY28 with domestic demand ramping from mid-CY27.

rows.label: Battery equity raise and debt funding
rows.why: About INR3,200 crore already raised (INR2,300 crore equity, INR900 crore debt); a further INR1,200 crore equity and INR1,500 crore debt remain, to be raised gradually with no parent backstop.

rows.label: LiPF6 price pass-through
rows.why: China LiPF6 prices reportedly fell from about INR150,000 to INR100,000 per tonne, and contracts are formula-linked to lithium with pass-through, so the margin read depends on pass-through lag.

tone.note: Management was confident on fluoropolymer growth (+22% YoY vs 17-20% guide) and R-32 volumes, but cautious and somewhat defensive on battery timelines and funding; analysts pushed on fluoropolymer sustainability, battery funding, and LiPF6 price pass-through.
